sources.title: New Observations on the Skull of Pyrotherium and New Phylogenetic Hypotheses on South American Ungulates
sources.author: Guillaume Billet, online2009, J Mammal Evol17:21-59(2010)
sources.evidence: Actual Fig1 ACM3207 dorsal/ventral/lateral skull with10cmbar and Fig13 skull/mandible occlusion photo viewed. Two upper tusk pairs and one lower pair, retracted nasal aperture. Author infers large proboscis, length unpreserved.

sources.title: The Deseado Formation of Patagonia, chapter XII
sources.author: Frederic Brewster Loomis (1914), Amherst College
sources.evidence: ACM3207 skull720mm incisor1-condyles and350mm zygomaticwidth; isolatedACM3218humerus470mm, citedGaudryradius245mm/femur630mm/tibia370mm. Historic sorondoi synonym now romeroi. Historical taxonomy/ancestry not adopted.
sources.rights: 1914 monograph public domain in US; research reference.

sources.title: Pyrotherium macfaddeni and pedal morphology of pyrotheres
sources.author: Shockey and Anaya (2004)
sources.evidence: Genus comparative tarsus supports graviportal plantigrade locomotion. P.macfaddeni smaller than romeroi, not same specimen. Historic assigned manus actually astrapothere; avoid fake complete foot anatomy.
sources.rights: Society of Vertebrate Paleontology/authors, text only.

sources.title: New Anatomical Data on Pyrotherium from Late Oligocene Mendoza
sources.author: Cerdeño and Vera (2017)
sources.evidence: Scattered carpal and calcaneal remains tentatively assigned to romeroi, taxonomic assignment limited by incomplete comparative record.
